# `.` — Inner product

`X f.g Y` pairs items with `g`, then reduces with `f`. It contracts the last axis of `X` with the first of `Y`.

```apl
1 2 3+.×4 5 6      ⍝ 32
[1 0 ⋄ 0 1]+.×2 2⍴⍳4 ⍝ 2 2⍴⍳4
```

Singleton contraction axes extend. Empty contractions use the reduction identity. `g⌝` is [outer product](outer-product.qmd).

After an array, `.name` reads a [keyed array](../keyed.qmd) value: `T.name` is `'name'⊃T`. It also works as an assignment target. Plain assignment creates missing records along the path.

```apl
T←('n':1 ⋄ 'addr':('city':'LA'))
T.addr.city        ⍝ 'LA'
T.n+←1 ⋄ T.n       ⍝ 2
```
